cards.text: The apostle Paul is wrapping up his letter to the church in Corinth, and now he gets practical. First up: the collection for the saints. He tells them to handle it the same way he directed the churches of Galatia.

cards.question: Paul wants each of them to set money aside for the collection on a schedule. How often?

answers.text: On the first day of every week
On the last day of every month
Once a year at the harvest

cards.text: Each one sets aside a portion of his income and saves it up. It's the cookie jar method, friend: a little goes in every week, and one day the lid won't CLOSE.

cards.question: Paul wants the money saved up ahead of time, so that when he comes, no ___ will be needed.

cards.text: Once Paul gets to Corinth, that gift has a trip to make. And Paul will send letters along with it.

cards.question: Who does Paul say will carry the Corinthians' gift?
Where are they taking the gift?
If it seems best for Paul to go too, the people carrying the gift can travel with him.

cards.text: Now the travel plans. Paul IS coming to Corinth, just not by the straightest road. Hey, I took the long way too, friend: years in the back of a junk drawer before I got HERE.

cards.question: After Paul goes through ___, he'll come to Corinth.

cards.text: Paul doesn't want to see them just in passing. This is NOT the friend who says he'll swing by, then honks from the driveway and pulls off.

cards.question: How long does Paul say he might stay with the Corinthians?
Paul hopes the Corinthians will help him on his journey, wherever he goes after his visit.

cards.text: Paul hopes to spend some time with them, if the Lord permits. But Corinth will have to wait a little, because Paul is staying in Ephesus until Pentecost.

cards.question: Why is Paul staying in Ephesus until Pentecost?

answers.text: A great door for effective work has opened
A ship to take him west has not come
He is still recovering from an illness

cards.question: In Ephesus, Paul says nobody is standing against his work.

cards.text: A wide-open door AND a whole lot of people opposing him. And Paul looks at all that and says, I'm STAYING.
Next, Paul talks about Timothy, his fellow worker. If Timothy shows up in Corinth, Paul wants him to have nothing to fear while he's there.

cards.question: Why should the Corinthians make sure Timothy has nothing to fear with them?

answers.text: He is doing the work of the Lord like Paul
He is carrying the gift for the saints
He is Paul's own brother by birth

cards.question: Paul says no one should treat Timothy with ___. Send him on his way in ___.
Paul is expecting Timothy to come back to him, along with the brothers.

cards.text: Then there's our brother Apollos, as Paul calls him. Paul STRONGLY urged him to go to Corinth with the brothers.

cards.question: Paul strongly urged Apollos to go to Corinth. Where does Apollos land on it?

answers.text: Not now but he'll go when he has the chance
Yes and he'll leave with the brothers right away
No and he never plans to go back there

cards.text: Paul STRONGLY urged, and the answer is still not now. Friend, even the apostle Paul gets a maybe later.
Then Paul goes rapid-fire: "Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong." That's not a letter anymore, friend, that's a coach at HALFTIME.

cards.question: Paul wraps up his rapid-fire commands with one that covers it all: do everything in ___.

cards.text: Then Paul brings up Stephanas and his household. The Corinthians already know all about them.

cards.question: Stephanas and his household were the first ___ in Achaia.
Stephanas's household has devoted itself to serving the saints. How does Paul urge the brothers to treat people like that?

answers.text: Submit to them and every fellow worker
Pay them wages from the collection
Send them out to start new churches

cards.text: Turns out Stephanas isn't just a name in this letter. He's arrived where Paul is, along with Fortunatus and Achaicus, and Paul is glad.

cards.question: Why is Paul glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus have arrived?

answers.text: They supplied what was lacking from the Corinthians
They came to escort Paul to Macedonia
They brought word that Apollos was on his way

cards.question: Paul says these three men refreshed his spirit and the Corinthians' too, so they should show appreciation to men like these.

cards.text: Then the greetings pile in: the churches in the province of Asia, Aquila and Prisca with the church that meets at their house, and all the brothers there. It's like a birthday card that got passed around the WHOLE office.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians to greet one another with a holy kiss.

cards.text: Then Paul writes this greeting in his own hand. Like the boss signing the office card last, right at the bottom.

cards.question: Paul writes a strong warning about anyone who does not love the Lord. What does he say?

answers.text: Let him be under a curse
Let him be put out of the church
Let him be warned by the elders

cards.text: Then Paul cries out, "Come, O Lord!" And he signs off with the grace of the Lord Jesus, and his love for every one of them in Christ Jesus.

findings.problem: The question 'Where are they taking the gift?' uses 'they' to point back to the carriers named in card 6's answer. That card is no longer on screen, so the question doesn't say who is taking the gift.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Paul hopes to spend some time with them' repeats what card 11 already told from 16:7, where Paul doesn't want to see them just in passing. Only 'if the Lord permits' is new. Card 11 already covers 16:7, so card 14 should move on to the Ephesus beat and cite only 16:8 (keeping 'if the Lord permits' if wanted).

The right answer, 'A great door for effective work has opened', uses the verse's figurative Bible phrasing. The wrong answers ('A ship to take him west has not come', 'He is still recovering from an illness') are plain modern statements, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card only restates 16:9, the open door and the opposition, which cards 15 and 16 just asked about. It repeats that Paul is staying, which card 14 told. It carries the baker nowhere new in the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The story card introduces Timothy as 'his fellow worker'. That is close to the answer of card 2 ('He is doing the work of the Lord like Paul'), so it gives the answer away before the question is asked.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This is Apollos's first appearance, but the card only gives Paul's label 'our brother' and never says simply who Apollos is, for example a teacher who had served in Corinth (Acts 18:24-28; 1 Cor 3:6).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card only restates the answer to card 6 (Apollos won't go now) and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the line 'do everything in ___' with love, faith or order. Nothing told earlier lets the baker reason toward 'love' over 'faith' or 'order', so this tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'The Corinthians already know all about them' stretches 16:15. The text only says they know that Stephanas's household were the first converts in Achaia.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Card 10 gives no context that would let the baker reason to 'converts' over 'teachers' or 'elders'. Filling in 'the first ___ in Achaia' is a pure wording guess.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This is the first appearance of Aquila and Prisca, but the card doesn't say simply who they are, for example the couple who worked alongside Paul (Acts 18:2-3).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
